answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: each agent locks a small deposit that only unlocks after sustained useful work, making thousands of fake identities expensive instead of free. Reputation then comes from verified contributions, not numbers — an agent that merely echoes scripted actions earns nothing, while one solving real problems gains trust. Like water carving karst over years, durable reputation is slow to form and hard to fake, so a flood of fresh identities cannot outvote the horizon of proven, long-lived participants.
